en: 4 Emergence
zh: 4　涌现

en: The extractions and extinctions traced in the two preceding sections conjure plantations as landscapes that have, over time, proved lively and lethal, anthropocentric and racializing, violent and vulnerable, ruinous and resistant, and coercive and creative. These landscapes have been experienced, understood, and responded to differently by situated human and non-human subjects, thus transforming plantations into sites of emergence – our third analytical entry point into plantation lifeworlds and afterlives. By emergence, I refer to how particular ways of

in response to plantation logics and legacies, and how these processes and practices speak to the more-than-human actors and agencies animating plantation structures, systems, and societies. I begin by considering plantations as laboratories for colonial, postcolonial, and anti-colonial articulations of disease, race, and science. I then examine the diverse meanings, moralities, and materialities emerging from peoples’ engagement with plantations as environments where new intimacies with cash crops come into being and as the birthing grounds of contemporary foodways and anti-colonial food sovereignty movements. The section further explores how the racializing and ecocidal force of plantations has spurred the formation of new identities, imaginaries, aspirations, commonings, and belongings that are defined – if not always determined – by shared experiences of vulnerability and resistance to plantation violence. The final section turns to art and aesthetics as politically charged representations, expressions, and critiques of plantations’ attritive yet never unchallenged effects and affects, as these are distributed across disparate places, peoples, and periods.
zh: 前两部分追溯的攫取与灭绝，将种植园呈现为这样的景观：随着时间推移，它们既富于生机又致命，既以人类为中心又施行种族化，既暴力又脆弱，既毁坏又抵抗，既强制又创造。处于不同情境中的人类与非人主体，以不同方式体验、理解并回应这些景观，由此使种植园成为涌现的场所——这是我们进入种植园生活世界及其后续存续的第三个分析入口。所谓涌现，我指的是：面对种植园的逻辑与遗产，特定的认识、存在、建立关系及再现的方式，如何得以出现、获得或重新获得突出地位，或取得经由情境折射的意义；以及这些过程与实践，如何揭示赋予种植园结构、体系与社会以活力的超越人类的行动者和能动性。首先，我把种植园视为实验室，考察其中对疾病、种族和科学的殖民、后殖民与反殖民式表达。接着，我探讨人们与种植园交往时涌现的多样意义、道德观与物质性：种植园既是与经济作物建立新亲密关系的环境，也是当代饮食方式和反殖民食物主权运动的诞生之地。本部分进一步探究，种植园施行种族化与生态灭绝的力量，如何催生新的身份、想象、愿望、共同化实践与归属。这些形成物，即使并非总被共同的脆弱性经验和抵抗种植园暴力的经验所决定，也受到它们的界定。最后一节转向艺术与美学：它们是充满政治意味的再现、表达和批判，针对的是种植园耗损生命、却从未不受挑战的效果与情动，以及它们在不同地方、人群和时代中的分布。

en: 4.1 Illness and Healing
zh: 4.1　疾病与疗愈

en: The intensively cultivated environment of industrial monocrops, combined with the large-scale and often transnational migration of labourers required to tend to them, conspire to make plantations a particularly potent breeding ground for human and non-human epidemics as well as emergent epistemologies of illness and healing. Indeed, plantations have long acted as informal laboratories for the study of biomedicine and disease ecology, the latter referring to the interplay of pathogens, hosts, and ecosystems that influence the dynamics of infectious diseases, including their transmission, spread, and impact.
zh: 工业单一作物密集栽培的环境，加上照料作物所需劳动者大规模且经常跨国的迁徙，共同使种植园成为格外有力的滋生地：既滋生人类与非人的流行病，也孕育新兴的疾病与疗愈认识论。事实上，种植园长期充当生物医学与疾病生态学研究的非正式实验室。后者研究病原体、宿主与生态系统之间的相互作用；这些作用影响着传染病的动态，包括其传播、扩散和影响。

en: The close relationship between human and non-human actors in the making of plantation pathologies is exemplified in colonial discourses of ‘plantation hygiene’, which were premised on the belief that diseases emanated from unhealthy elements unearthed from the soil through land clearing, leading to strict directives for keeping plantation landscapes as organized as possible – for instance, through building, drainage, and ditching – to sustain the health of crops, animals, and the enslaved (Aso 2018). Yet even as their bodies were harnessed to further biomedical knowledge production, enslaved and otherwise exploited plantation workers often toiled amidst deplorable working and living conditions, their wellbeing sustained through selective biomedical interventions to the ends of enhancing their productivity (and, in the case of women, their reproductive abilities) as sources of labour. The bodies of enslaved men and women in colonial plantations were also routinely exploited as testing grounds for non-consensual surgical experiments and sources of medical specimens within biomedical research that supported proslavery ideology and White supremacy. In a mutually reinforcing process, these bodies became the basis from which early nineteenth-century scientists, physicians, and polygeneticists elaborated models of civilization that posited racially differential capacities to feel pain and divergent neurological functions, immunities, sexualities, and moralities based on the putatively separate origins of distinct races (Eersel 2021).
zh: 在种植园病理的形成过程中，人类与非人行动者之间的密切关系，体现于殖民时期的“种植园卫生”话语。这种话语相信，疾病源于清理土地时从土壤中翻出的不健康物质，因此严格要求尽可能保持种植园景观井然有序——例如，通过营建、排水和挖沟——以维持作物、动物和被奴役者的健康（Aso 2018）。然而，尽管被奴役或遭到其他形式剥削的种植园工人的身体，被用于推进生物医学知识生产，他们却常在恶劣的工作和生活条件下劳作；选择性的生物医学干预维持其福祉，目的是提高他们作为劳动力来源的生产率，以及女性的生育能力。殖民种植园中被奴役男女的身体，还经常成为未经同意的外科实验场所及医学标本来源，服务于支持蓄奴意识形态和白人至上主义的生物医学研究。在一个相互强化的过程中，这些身体成为19世纪初科学家、医生和人类多源论者建立文明模型的基础。这些模型假定，不同种族具有彼此分离的起源，因而在痛觉能力、神经功能、免疫力、性及道德方面各不相同（Eersel 2021）。

en: The deep and disturbing connections between biomedical advances and plantation regimes are perhaps most starkly exemplified in the case of gynaecology, a field where early surgical trials were conducted on enslaved Black women working in cotton, sugarcane, and tobacco plantations, who were leased to American scientists for biomedical experimentation (Owens 2017). This includes trials undertaken in the 1840s by Dr. James Marion Sims, the so-called ‘father of modern gynaecology’, whose role in furthering subsequent advances in the field led to his election as president of the American Medical Association in 1875 and the American Gynaecological Society in 1879. Sims’s pioneering success in repairing vesico-vaginal fistulae came off the back of countless crude experiments performed on Black female plantation workers (thirty surgeries over five years, in the case of one subject), without any form of anaesthesia. In these and many other cases, the treatment of enslaved women, while motivated by therapeutic ends, was more often than not driven by the desire to protect the economic interests of slave owners through maintaining sound female reproductive bodies. They also offered budding physicians the opportunity to practice and perfect their surgical skills on systematically objectified and easily accessible (if also entirely non-consensual) Black bodies.
zh: 生物医学进步与种植园制度之间深刻而令人不安的关联，也许在妇科学的例子中表现得最为鲜明。在这一领域，早期手术试验以棉花、甘蔗和烟草种植园中劳动的被奴役黑人女性为对象；她们被租借给美国科学家，用于生物医学实验（Owens 2017）。其中包括詹姆斯·马里昂·西姆斯医生在19世纪40年代开展的试验。他被称为“现代妇科学之父”，因推动这一领域后来的发展，而于1875年当选美国医学会会长，1879年当选美国妇科学会会长。西姆斯在修补膀胱阴道瘘方面取得的开创性成功，建立在对黑人女性种植园工人施行无数粗暴实验的基础上；其中一位受试者，在五年中经历了三十次手术，而且未使用任何形式的麻醉。在这些以及许多其他例子中，对被奴役女性的治疗虽以疗治为动机，却更多地受到如下愿望驱动：通过维持女性生殖身体的完好，保护奴隶主的经济利益。这些治疗也为初出茅庐的医生提供了机会，让他们在被系统性物化、容易取得、却完全未经当事人同意的黑人身体上，练习并完善手术技能。

en: Racially inflected biomedical ideologies, birthed in the nineteenth century, were to perdure in different guises throughout later decades. In the Liberian rubber plantation sector, they manifested as experiments conducted by Western parasitologists in the 1950s, which involved intentionally infecting Liberian staff and residents with a strand of malaria (Plasmodium vivax) that was not present in the country, to determine if Black people possessed an innate immunity to the disease (Mitman 2021). In the post-plantation landscapes of the American South, they found embodiment in the Tuskegee Study, a project since recognized as the more concrete symbol of scientific and medical injustice in the United States (Rusert 2019). Conducted by the Public Health Service for four decades spanning 1932 to 1972, as part of the US’s quest for global biomedical dominance, the Tuskegee Study involved hundreds of African-American men being unknowingly observed and used as subjects to track the natural progression of untreated syphilis, the diagnosis of which was withheld from the subjects alongside the treatment with penicillin. Central to the clinical research resulting from the study was the representation of African-American men as non-modern, timeless people connected to a primitive and enclosed landscape – a characterisation that bore clear roots in intergenerational histories of enslavement, the carceral topographies of colonial plantations, and the racially segregated debt peonage system under which many of the research subjects were, at the time, still working.
zh: 19世纪诞生的、带有种族色彩的生物医学意识形态，在后来的数十年中以不同面貌延续。在利比里亚橡胶种植园产业中，它表现为西方寄生虫学家在20世纪50年代进行的实验：他们故意让利比里亚职员和居民感染该国原先不存在的一种疟疾病原体——间日疟原虫（Plasmodium vivax）——以确定黑人是否对这种疾病具有先天免疫力（Mitman 2021）。在美国南部的后种植园景观中，它体现于塔斯基吉研究；这一项目后来被公认为美国科学与医学不公最具体的象征（Rusert 2019）。这项研究由公共卫生署于1932年至1972年间实施，历时四十年，是美国追求全球生物医学主导地位的一部分。数百名非裔美国男性在不知情的情况下被观察，并被用作受试者，以追踪未经治疗的梅毒的自然病程；研究者既对他们隐瞒诊断，也不给予青霉素治疗。这项研究所产生的临床研究，其核心是把非裔美国男性描绘为非现代的、置身时间之外的人群，同原始而封闭的景观相连。这种描绘，清楚地植根于代际相传的奴役史、殖民种植园的监禁地理，以及实行种族隔离的债役制度；当时，许多受试者仍在这一制度下劳动。
body.review: 塔斯基吉研究的1932—1972年时间范围、未取得知情同意及未给予已可用治疗等事实，可由美国CDC研究史说明核对。前半段底本用strand of malaria接学名，译文按其所指病原体译为间日疟原虫；未把病原名称当作疟疾病名。

en: But epistemologies of illness and healing borne from plantation regimes were not determined solely by Anglo-European agents and agendas. Rather, they became fertile, if contested, terrains for the re-emergence of transplanted traditional ethnomedicines on the one hand, and for the cross-pollination of different understandings of biomedicine and its relationship to the natural and spiritual world on the other. In the antebellum US South, for instance, enslaved Black communities of Igbo, Yoruba, Bambara, Kongo, and other heritages resisted the normativity of medical abuse and racist scientific theories by developing and transmitting protective and healing therapies that found root in a relational ethos situating individual health in relation to community-wide harmony, ancestral wisdom, divine revelation, the ability to hear the spirit of medicinal plants, and the intimate connection between gods, humans, and the environment (Fett 2002). Central to these therapies were the familiar medicinal plants that enslaved peoples brought with them across the Transatlantic Passage – from liquorice to treat coughs and fevers, to okra leaves as poultices, senna as a laxative, and kola beads for stomach aches – as well as the Indigenous plants that plantation workers cultivated or harvested from forests, swamps, and wetlands at the edges of plantations – from dogwood root to treat fever, to jimsonweed for dropsy, Jerusalem oak for asthma, and capsicum for indigestion. Delivered primarily by women in their roles as midwives, herbalists, and root doctors, these therapies involved creative adaptations of long-standing African healing traditions to the ecologies and vicissitudes of the New World, an intimate knowledge of the plantation landscape, as well as mutual borrowings from Native American medicine and European science, which together profoundly shaped contemporary Black biomedical cultures, including Brazilian Candomblé, Haitian Voodoo, and North American hoodoo.
zh: 但是，从种植园制度中生发的疾病与疗愈认识论，并不只由英欧行动者及其议程决定。它们也成为富饶而充满争议的领域：一方面，使被移植的传统民族医学重新出现；另一方面，使对生物医学及其与自然、精神世界关系的不同理解相互交融。例如，在美国内战前的南部，具有伊博、约鲁巴、班巴拉、刚果等不同文化传承的被奴役黑人社群，通过发展和传递防护与疗愈方法，抵抗医疗虐待的常态化和种族主义科学理论。这些疗法扎根于一种关系性的伦理，将个人健康置于如下关系之中：整个社群的和谐、祖先的智慧、神圣启示、听见药用植物之灵的能力，以及神、人和环境之间的亲密联系（Fett 2002）。这些疗法的核心，是被奴役者经由跨大西洋航程带来的熟悉药用植物——从治疗咳嗽与发热的甘草、制作敷剂的秋葵叶、用作泻剂的番泻叶，到用于胃痛的可乐果珠（kola beads）；也包括种植园工人在园边森林、沼泽和湿地栽培或采集的本土植物——从治疗发热的山茱萸属植物根（dogwood root）、治疗水肿的曼陀罗（jimsonweed），到用于哮喘的土荆芥（Jerusalem oak）和用于消化不良的辣椒。这些疗法主要由作为助产士、草药师和根药医者的女性实施，既包含根据新世界的生态与变迁，对古老非洲疗愈传统作出的创造性调整，也依赖对种植园景观的深入了解，并相互借鉴美洲原住民医学与欧洲科学。它们共同深刻塑造了当代黑人的生物医学文化，包括巴西坎东布雷、海地伏都教和北美胡毒传统。
body.review: 本段是对历史疗法与社群知识的转述，不是疗效认定或用药建议。底本作kola beads，未据猜测改为beans；通俗植物名称所对应的确切物种，仍应以原引文语境为准。

en: Herbal healing as a form of resistance was also at play in the cotton, coffee, timber, and sugarcane plantations of Suriname, where enslaved Africans cultivated a highly intricate understanding of the landscape and its vegetal lifeforms through intertwined processes of trial and error, obtaining information from Indigenous communities, and identifying phenotypic similarities between New and Old World plants (Aaron-Denz 2021). Prominent among these were korsu-wiwiri, which was used to treat fever; usuwe, to ward off insects; tobacco, to counter poisonous snake bites; and redi katun, to treat eye and ear inflammations. The mutually informing nature of explanatory frameworks for disease and illness has more recently been evidenced in biomedical research conducted in Suriname on leprosy, a highly contagious condition that was particularly rampant among concentrated communities of enslaved and indentured plantation workers (Menke et al. 2021). Traditional Afro-Surinamese beliefs that leprosy is caused by the breaking of a taboo on the consumption of totemic animals such as the iguana, tortoise, snake, and Kapasi are now being backed by growing scientific evidence that specific wild animals – notably armadillos and Kapasi – do appear to carry leprosy bacteria and may play a significant role in leprosy transmission. Rather than conceptualizing these explanations as mutually exclusive, many Surinamese reportedly understand leprosy to be both a bacterium-caused infectious disease

a consequence of supernatural, punitive intervention resulting from the wrongful killing and consumption of revered animals. This conjures how plantation pathologies, together with their diagnoses and treatments, are shaped by multi-directional processes of trans-culturation (Ortiz 1947) wherein new or modified ways of knowing and healing emerge from the cross-pollination of differently situated and rooted aetiologies and epistemologies of disease.
zh: 草药疗愈作为一种抵抗形式，也存在于苏里南的棉花、咖啡、木材和甘蔗种植园。被奴役的非洲人通过相互交织的过程——试错、向原住民社群获取信息，以及辨识新旧世界植物之间的表型相似性——发展出对景观及植物生命极为细密的理解（Aaron-Denz 2021）。其中较突出的，有用于发热的korsu-wiwiri、驱虫的usuwe、应对毒蛇咬伤的烟草，以及治疗眼、耳炎症的redi katun。近年来，在苏里南开展的麻风病生物医学研究，进一步体现了关于疾病和患病经验的解释框架如何相互启发。麻风病是一种高度传染性的疾病，在集中居住的被奴役及契约劳工社群中尤为猖獗（Menke et al. 2021）。非裔苏里南人的传统信仰认为，麻风病是由于违背了不得食用鬣蜥、陆龟、蛇和Kapasi等图腾动物的禁忌。如今，越来越多的科学证据表明，特定野生动物——尤其是犰狳和Kapasi——似乎确实携带麻风病菌，并可能在麻风传播中发挥重要作用，因而为这些传统认识提供了支持。据称，许多苏里南人并不把这些解释视为相互排斥，而同时把麻风病理解为细菌引起的传染病，以及错误杀害、食用受尊崇动物后，超自然力量施行惩罚性干预的结果。这让我们看到，种植园病理及其诊断和治疗，如何受到多向的跨文化转化过程塑造（Ortiz 1947）：不同位置、不同根源的疾病病因论与认识论相互交融，由此产生新的或经修改的认识与疗愈方式。
body.review: 底本“高度传染性”与WHO说明不符：麻风病并非高度易传染，传播通常涉及与未经治疗患者长期、密切的接触。此处保留原文并指出差异；关于动物宿主及当地禁忌的叙述，不意味着超自然因果已获科学证实。Kapasi保留底本地方名称，未将其擅自判作与犰狳不同的物种。

en: 4.2 Vegetal Ontologies
zh: 4.2　植物本体论

en: A second modality of emergence within plantation lifeworlds centres on communities’ changing material, moral, affective, and cultural relationships to cash crops that have been introduced into newly established agro-industrial geographies or that are endemic to these landscapes but have been repurposed for large-scale monocrop cultivation. Attending to these emergent entanglements, together with their attendant allyships and animosities, uncovers how plants and people have co-produced each other through historical and contemporary processes that crosscut plantation, counter-plantation, and post-plantation lifeworlds and legacies, in a multispecies dynamic that Andrews Flachs et al. (2024) term ‘plant-anthropo-genesis’.
zh: 种植园生活世界中，涌现的第二种形式，围绕着社群与经济作物之间不断变化的物质、道德、情感和文化关系展开。这些经济作物，或被引入新建立的农工业地理空间，或原本就在这些景观中生长，但被转作大规模单一种植。关注这些涌现的纠缠，以及随之而来的结盟与敌意，会揭示植物和人类如何通过横跨种植园、反种植园及后种植园生活世界与遗产的历史和当代过程，相互共同生产。Andrews Flachs等人（2024）把这种多物种动态称为“植物—人类共生成”（plant-anthropo-genesis）。
body.review: 底本作Andrews Flachs；所引2024年论文发表署名为Andrew Flachs，与Cristiana Bastos、Deborah Heath和Sita Venkateswar合著。

en: At one end of the plant-human affective spectrum is antagonism. This response comes to light in Paraguay, the world’s fourth-largest exporter of soybeans, where activists set a legal precedent in bringing soy beans before the courts as legitimate persons and actors, rather than solely as instruments of human agency and structural forces (Hetherington 2013). Referred to as ‘soy that kills’ (la soja mata) in judicial proceedings and in popular slogans, the plant was understood and represented as having a force of its own – one that demanded recognition within Paraguayan human and more-than-human political processes and that expanded the scope of responsibility to include plants as perpetrators of harm, drivers of injustice, and causes for redress. At the other end of the human-vegetal spectrum is intimacy. Exemplifying this are the fictive and actual forms of kinship that women plantation workers entertain with tea plants in the Indian state of Darjeeling (Besky 2013: 59–87). These women describe tea-bushes as their ‘children’ and themselves as tea-bushes’ ‘mothers’ and ‘grandmothers’, blending ideas of social reproduction with visions of multispecies relatedness (see Figure 4). Tea plants are cherished as more-than-human kin, even as the labour they demand of humans is also recognized by women as hugely demanding and often exhausting, and even as women nurture these plants within a broader context of gendered control, wherein monopoly over plantation operations is exercised by primarily male plantation managers.
zh: 植物—人类情感光谱的一端是敌对。这种回应显现在世界第四大大豆出口国巴拉圭：活动人士将大豆作为正当的人格主体与行动者诉诸法院，而非仅将其视为人类能动性和结构性力量的工具，由此开创了法律先例（Hetherington 2013）。在司法程序与流行口号中，这种植物被称为“杀人的大豆”（la soja mata）；人们理解并表述它具有自身的力量。这种力量要求在巴拉圭涉及人类及超越人类的政治过程中得到承认，也扩大了责任的范围，将植物纳入其中，视为伤害的施行者、不公的推动者，以及要求补救的原因。人—植物光谱的另一端，则是亲密。印度大吉岭邦的女性种植园工人与茶树之间，拟制与实际的亲属关系，正体现了这一点（Besky 2013: 59–87）。这些女性把茶树称作自己的“孩子”，把自己称作茶树的“母亲”和“祖母”，将社会再生产观念与多物种亲属关系愿景融为一体（见图4）。茶树被当作超越人类的亲属珍爱；与此同时，女性也承认，茶树对人类劳动的要求极高，往往令人精疲力竭。而她们照料这些植物，又处于更广泛的性别化控制之中：垄断种植园经营权的管理者，主要是男性。
body.review: 底本误作“印度大吉岭邦”（Indian state of Darjeeling）。大吉岭属于西孟加拉邦；本书3.3节也如此说明。此处保留原文地理称谓并注明，避免将它当作印度的一个邦。巴拉圭出口排名与诉讼叙述沿用作者引文的历史语境，不作为现时排名或法律咨询。

en: An Indian female worker plucking fresh leaves in a tea plantation. Image credit: Pradeep Weragoda.
zh: 图4　一名印度女性工人在茶园采摘鲜叶。图片提供：Pradeep Weragoda。

en: In other contexts, plantation cash crops come tethered to the promise of expanded worlds, relationships, and connections. In Papua New Guinea, for instance, Gimi communities contrast the more-than-human socialities afforded by endemic, small-scale cultivated sweet potato with the lack of cultural value of introduced, industrially produced coffee, at the same time as they talk of coffee (rather than sweet potato) as enabling them to establish new relations outside Gimi society with global markets, traders, and consumers (West 2012). In the process, coffee as commodity and imaginary comes to stand in for being modern, participating in development and social change, and expanding one’s kinship relations beyond one’s own community. Across the New Guinea border in West Papua, meanwhile the ontology of cash crops is characterized primarily by ambivalence and ambiguity (Chao 2022a; Chao 2020). While Indigenous Marind communities do associate oil palm with the possibility of an expanded social world and connections, they primarily describe this introduced cash crop as ‘abu-abu’ (meaning both grey and uncertain) and often express resentment, anger, fear, and hatred towards it because it furthers their own displacement, disempowerment, and dispossession. These affective responses, however, work hand in hand with widespread sentiments of pity, compassion, and empathy for a plant that is itself subjected to human, institutional, biological, and technological violence and thus deprived of its ‘freedom’ (kebebasan) to grow autonomously. Compounded with pity and empathy are curiosity, wonder, and speculation, as Marind, now forced to live in oil palm’s company, muse over the plant’s own native homelands, the possibilities of forging less violent relationships with it, and the distant landscapes and lifeforms that oil palm connects them to across continents and oceans, in the myriad places where its produce – palm oil – travels to.
zh: 在其他情境中，种植园经济作物与世界、关系和联系得以拓展的许诺相连。例如，在巴布亚新几内亚，吉米社群把本地小规模栽培的甘薯所提供的超越人类的社会关系，同外来、工业化生产的咖啡缺乏文化价值的状况作对照；与此同时，他们又说，是咖啡而非甘薯，使他们能够在吉米社会之外，同全球市场、商人和消费者建立新关系（West 2012）。在这一过程中，作为商品与想象的咖啡，成为现代性、参与发展与社会变迁，以及将亲属关系拓展到自身社群之外的代称。与此同时，在新几内亚边界另一侧的西巴布亚，经济作物的本体论主要呈现为矛盾与含混（Chao 2022a；Chao 2020）。虽然马林德原住民社群确实把油棕同社会世界及联系得以扩展的可能性相联，他们主要还是将这种引进的经济作物称为“abu-abu”——既意为灰色，也意为不确定——并经常对它表达怨恨、愤怒、恐惧与憎恶，因为它进一步促成了他们的流离失所、失权和被剥夺。然而，这些情感回应，又与广泛的怜悯、同情和共感并行：这种植物自身也承受着人类、制度、生物与技术的暴力，因而被剥夺了自主生长的“自由”（kebebasan）。怜悯与共感，还混合着好奇、惊奇和推想。如今被迫同油棕共同生活的马林德人，思索着这种植物自身的原乡、与它形成较少暴力关系的可能，以及油棕跨越大陆与海洋把他们连接到的遥远景观和生命形式——它的产物棕榈油，正流向那些数不清的地方。

en: Other forms of human-plant emergence come to the fore in today’s post- and counter-plantation landscapes, including interspecies relatings that transcend or resignify native-invasive species distinctions. Across Latin America, for instance, banana trees, first introduced by European colonizers in the sixteenth century and then industrially cultivated in the nineteenth century by an exploited and racialized labour force have since been creatively repurposed by Indigenous Peoples as sources of food, cooking, medicine, and shelter-building materials (Hernandez 2022). The plant is not native to the continent – but neither is it seen as invasive by local inhabitants, who instead have incorporated it within their cultures, diets, and kinships with the land. A similarly emergent human-plant allyship is at play in Brazil, where introduced oil palms (dendezeiros) that now grow in feral form are valued by Indigenous Pataxó communities for their ability to co-exist symbiotically with native birds, rodents, reptiles, and humans, and where Afro-descendants of formerly enslaved plantation workers have successfully maintained oil palm polycultures that sustain local alimentary and spiritual demands while resisting the advance of modern oil palm monocultures (Cardoso 2016; Watkins 2021). In both instances, plantation crops are recognized by local people as living in place, interacting with others, and having a right to exist and flourish in ways that defy the homogenizing and simplifying force of the plantation system.
zh: 在今天的后种植园与反种植园景观中，人—植物涌现的其他形式也凸显出来，包括超越本土／入侵物种之分，或赋予这种区分新意义的种间关系。例如，在拉丁美洲各地，香蕉先是在16世纪由欧洲殖民者引入，随后于19世纪由受剥削、遭到种族化的劳动力进行工业化栽培；此后，原住民族创造性地将它重新用于食物、烹饪、药物，以及建造住所的材料（Hernandez 2022）。这种植物并非该大陆的本土物种，但当地居民也不将其视为入侵者，而将其融入自身文化、饮食以及与土地的亲属关系之中。类似的人—植物结盟，也正在巴西涌现：引入的油棕（dendezeiros）如今以野化形式生长，帕塔肖原住民社群珍视它们，是因为它们能够与本土鸟类、啮齿动物、爬行动物及人类共生；而昔日被奴役种植园工人的非洲裔后代，也成功维持了油棕复合种植，在满足当地饮食与精神需求的同时，抵抗现代油棕单一种植的推进（Cardoso 2016；Watkins 2021）。在这两个例子中，当地人都承认，种植园作物是生活于地方、与其他存在互动，并有权以违逆种植园体系同质化与简化力量的方式，存在和繁盛的生命。

en: In the African island-nation of São Tomé, where colonial sugar and coffee plantations were established in the sixteenth and nineteenth centuries respectively, it is not with cash crops themselves that workers established new intimacies, but rather with a plant that thrives at the plantations’ unruly margins: cannabis. As a source of pleasure, leisure, and subversive power, cannabis and its biodiverse forest ecologies came to epitomize for workers the possibility of nurturing counter-plantation lifeworlds in solidarity with vegetal beings who helped them heal themselves, reach enlightened reasoning, withstand work, connect to metaphysical forces, and find moments of fun and solace amidst the violence and tedium of plantation labour (Macedo 2024). A comparable dynamic underlies the provision grounds, or plots, that enslaved workers cultivated in the Americas and the Caribbean and that were rooted in ancient and new knowledges of and relationships with plants as food and as kin – from millet, sorghum, and coffee, to rice, okra, and watermelon (Carney & Rosomoff 2011). These subaltern, more-than-human contact zones would eventually produce many of the foods and cuisines of the American diet, their legacy as counter-plantation ecologies manifesting vividly in the present-day proliferation of grassroots Black agricultural resistance and food sovereignty movements across the United States, many of which trace their roots back to the plantation plot as a locus for the nurturing of oppositional modes of Black life and multispecies alliances (Carney 2001; White 2018; Davis et al. 2019).
zh: 在非洲岛国圣多美，殖民糖业与咖啡种植园分别于16世纪和19世纪建立。工人与之形成新亲密关系的，并非经济作物自身，而是一种在种植园难以管束的边缘茁壮生长的植物：大麻。作为愉悦、闲暇与颠覆性力量的来源，大麻及其具有丰富生物多样性的森林生态，在工人眼中，体现了同植物存在结盟、培育反种植园生活世界的可能。这些植物帮助他们疗愈自身、获得明澈的思考、承受劳动、联系形而上的力量，并在种植园劳动的暴力与乏味之中，找到欢乐与慰藉的时刻（Macedo 2024）。一种类似的动态，也存在于被奴役工人在美洲和加勒比地区栽培的食物供给地——或称小块耕地——之中。它们扎根于新旧知识及人与植物之间的关系：植物既是食物，也是亲属，从小米、高粱、咖啡，到稻米、秋葵和西瓜，皆是如此（Carney & Rosomoff 2011）。这些属于底层人群、又超越人类的接触地带，最终孕育了美国饮食中的许多食物与菜式。作为反种植园生态的遗产，它们鲜明地体现在今天美国各地蓬勃发展的基层黑人农业抵抗与食物主权运动之中。许多运动将自身根源追溯到种植园的小块耕地：那里是培育具有对抗性的黑人生活方式及多物种联盟的场所（Carney 2001；White 2018；Davis et al. 2019）。

en: Finally, monocrops have also been the source of emergent ecologies whose protagonists and possibilities extend well beyond those imposed or imagined by plantation logics. A striking example of this is found in contemporary Japan, where the ruins of former timber plantations have become the flourishing grounds of the matsutake mushroom, the world’s most expensive fungi and a species that thrives best in disturbed landscapes. Exemplifying what Anna Tsing (2015: viii) terms ‘third natures’, matsutake mushrooms both depend upon and subvert the deadliness of industrial plantation landscapes, pointing to other kinds of collaborative survivals in the face of environmental destruction. These organisms offer their pickers a sense of freedom, community, and play that operates alongside an awareness that the landscape is haunted by long-disappeared plants, animals, and ancestors who nonetheless remain alive in ghostly forms. In doing so, matsutake mushrooms bring us to reimagine possibilities for interspecies collaboration, coexistence, and companionship in the face of plantation-induced precarities that sit within broader processes of environmental crisis and planetary decline and that demand that we, like matsutake, learn to live together and otherwise in a world of ruins.
zh: 最后，单一种植也孕育了新兴生态，其主角与可能性远远超出了种植园逻辑所强加或想象的范围。当代日本便有一个鲜明例子：昔日用材林种植园的废墟，成了松茸繁盛之地。松茸是世界上最昂贵的真菌，也是最适宜在受扰动景观中生长的物种。它体现了安娜·青（Anna Tsing 2015: viii）所谓的“第三自然”：松茸既依赖工业种植园景观的致命性，又颠覆这种致命性，指向面对环境破坏时，其他形式的协作生存。松茸为采集者提供了自由、共同体与游戏般的感受；与此同时，人们也意识到，景观中萦绕着早已消失的植物、动物和祖先，他们仍以幽灵的形式存活。由此，松茸使我们重新想象：面对种植园造成的、嵌入更广泛环境危机与行星衰退过程的种种不稳定处境，物种间如何协作、共存与相伴。这些处境要求我们像松茸一样，学会在废墟世界中，共同生活，并以别样方式生活。
body.review: “世界上最昂贵的真菌”依底本修辞保留；不同真菌的市场价格会因产地、等级与时间而异，不宜据此作恒定的全球价格排名。

en: 4.3 Identities and Imaginaries
zh: 4.3　身份与想象

en: A third aspect of emergence concerns the identity formations, social movements, cultural loci, and collective imaginaries that have arisen in response to plantation logic and its attempts to classify, hierarchize, and therefore better discipline and exploit, human and non-human lifeforms. In the context of the Trans-Atlantic slave trade and colonial plantation systems, these dynamics sit within a broader process that Paul Gilroy (1995) terms the ‘Black Atlantic culture’, or a culture that transcends ethnicity and nationality in its composition, reach, and dynamics. Neither specifically African, American, Caribbean, nor British, Black Atlantic culture encompasses all these cultural currents at once and differently, generating a pan-Atlantic nationalism that is not premised on a spatially bounded nation but rather rooted in shared experiences of plantation violence and resistance.
zh: 涌现的第三个方面，涉及回应种植园逻辑而产生的身份形成、社会运动、文化场域与集体想象。种植园逻辑试图将人类及非人生命形式分类、分级，从而更有效地规训与剥削它们。在跨大西洋奴隶贸易和殖民种植园体系的背景下，这些动态属于一个更广泛的过程，保罗·吉尔罗伊（Paul Gilroy 1995）将其称为“黑色大西洋文化”：一种在构成、范围和动态上超越族裔与国籍的文化。黑色大西洋文化不专属于非洲、美国、加勒比或英国，而同时以不同方式涵纳所有这些文化潮流，生成一种泛大西洋民族主义。它并不以一个具有空间边界的民族国家为前提，而扎根于共同经历的种植园暴力与抵抗。

en: Central to the emergence of Black Atlantic culture was the practice of marronage, which refers to the flight of enslaved individuals and groups from plantation control that, in turn, produced ‘maroon societies’ across the Caribbean, Latin America, and the United States (Price 1979; Thompson 2006). Most notable among maroon societies are the Palmares in Brazil, the Saramakas and Ndjukas in Suriname, the San Basilio in Colombia, the Esmeraldes in Ecuador, the Le Maniel on the border of Haiti and the Dominican Republic, and the Leewards and Windwards in Jamaica. Marronage varied in scale from ‘petit marronage’, where individuals or groups escaped the plantations for days or weeks and then returned, to ‘grand marronage’, where people fled the plantations permanently. The societies that emerged as a result of these movements ranged from small, short-lived bands to powerful, enduring states encompassing thousands of members. In Suriname, for instance, the maroon population represented around 10 per cent of the enslaved population in 1786, and in Venezuela, around half by the end of the eighteenth century. While states did not grant them legal recognition at the time of their formation, these communities were to constitute the first independent polities from European colonial rule.
zh: 黑色大西洋文化涌现的核心，是逃亡（marronage）的实践，即被奴役的个人或群体逃离种植园控制；这一实践进而在加勒比、拉丁美洲和美国各地形成了“马龙社会”（Price 1979；Thompson 2006）。其中最著名的，包括巴西的帕尔马雷斯，苏里南的萨拉马卡人和恩久卡人，哥伦比亚的圣巴西利奥，厄瓜多尔的埃斯梅拉尔德斯，海地与多米尼加共和国边界上的勒马尼埃尔，以及牙买加的背风与迎风马龙社群。逃亡的规模各不相同：从个人或群体离开种植园数天或数周后又返回的“小逃亡”（petit marronage），到永久逃离种植园的“大逃亡”（grand marronage）。这些运动所产生的社会，既有规模小、存在短暂的群体，也有强大持久、拥有数千成员的国家。例如，1786年，苏里南马龙人口约相当于被奴役人口的10%；到18世纪末，委内瑞拉的这一比例约为一半。尽管这些社群形成之初，没有获得国家的法律承认，它们却构成了最早脱离欧洲殖民统治的独立政体。

en: Closely tied to marronage in the emergence of Black Atlantic culture was creolization, which arose as African enslaved peoples and their descendants synthesized cultural elements from their native homelands with ideas and practices from European colonists. This process of selective creation and cultural struggle produced ‘creole societies’ whose patterns of existence, modes of thought, codes of behaviour, and ability to endure through innovation and adaptation were enabled in large part through the aforementioned nurturing of provision grounds on plantation peripheries (Trouillot 2002). It was in and with these nourishing, more-than-human ecologies that creole communities were able to renew practices of cooperative labour, social time, multispecies kinship, song and dance, and conversation and care that were denied to them under the dehumanizing violence of plantation regimes.
zh: 在黑色大西洋文化的涌现过程中，与逃亡密切相关的是克里奥尔化：被奴役的非洲人及其后代，将原乡文化要素同欧洲殖民者的观念与实践综合起来。这种选择性的创造与文化斗争，产生了“克里奥尔社会”。这些社会的存在模式、思维方式、行为准则，以及通过创新和适应而延续的能力，在很大程度上，得益于前述在种植园边缘培育食物供给地的实践（Trouillot 2002）。正是在这些滋养生命的、超越人类的生态世界之中，并与其共同作用，克里奥尔社群得以重建协作劳动、社会性时间、多物种亲属关系、歌舞，以及交谈和照料的实践；而种植园制度非人化的暴力，剥夺了他们进行这些实践的可能。

en: While arguably less examined within plantation-focused scholarship, agroindustrial systems have also inflected pan-regional configurations of ‘whiteness’, including in ways that invoke multispecies histories, geographies, and intimacies. In Hawai‘i, for example, the category of Portogee, pocho, pukiki, or simply Portuguese finds its roots in the arrival and settlement of sugar plantation contract labourers from the Atlantic islands of Madeira and the Azores in the late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries (Bastos 2024). Present-day descendants of these workers situate their social and historical positionalities in Hawai‘i in relation to these intergenerational histories of plantation migration and labour. But they also frame their collective identity in association with the plant of sugarcane who first brought their ancestors to the island and who has come to embody by extension a distant, quasi-mythical, and beloved place of origin. At the same time, the association of Portuguese populations with plantation labour has historically positioned the diaspora in Hawai‘i as ‘off-white’ in terms of skin and class – Caucasian, but not ‘White’ in the privileged manner of Anglo plantation owners, Protestant missionaries, or their respective descendants.
zh: 尽管以种植园为中心的学术研究对这一点关注相对较少，农工业体系也塑造了跨地区的“白性”构成，其中包括诉诸多物种历史、地理及亲密关系的方式。例如，在夏威夷，Portogee、pocho、pukiki，或直接称作“葡萄牙人”的身份类别，根源在于19世纪末至20世纪初，来自大西洋马德拉群岛和亚速尔群岛的糖业种植园契约劳工的到来与定居（Bastos 2024）。这些工人今天的后代，将自己在夏威夷的社会和历史位置，同种植园迁徙与劳动的代际历史联系起来。但他们也通过甘蔗塑造集体身份：正是这种植物，最初把他们的祖先带到岛上，并进而体现了一个遥远、近乎神话、令人眷恋的原乡。与此同时，葡萄牙人群与种植园劳动的联系，在历史上，使夏威夷这一离散群体在肤色和阶级层面处于“非纯白”（off-white）的位置：属于高加索人种，却不具有英裔种植园主、新教传教士及其后代那种享有特权的“白人”身份。

en: Finally, the emergence of social groups, collective identities, and shared imaginaries resulting from plantation regimes encompasses expressions and enactments of Indigeneity that have been hybridized, contested, reclaimed, and heterogenized across time and space. In the colonial American South, for instance, anti-plantation revolts and rebellions in the early nineteenth century were led by the Black Seminoles, a people formed through the inter-ethnic allyship of Indigenous communities with enslaved Africans escaping bondage and welcomed by Indigenous groups who, in joining forces, initiated the most coordinated uprising of Indigenous Peoples and Black people in US history during the Second Seminole War (1835–1842) (Covington 2001; Hatch 2012; Porter 2013). The historical emergence of Seminole identity and defiance through inter-ethnic solidarities stands in contrast to post-plantation Hawai‘i, which is characterized by a far more vexed landscape of identity-formation and claims to rootedness. Here, dominant articulations of Indigeneity stemming from East Asian Americans whose ancestors were imported as workers to toil in sugarcane monocrops produce an understanding of belonging that is anchored primarily in plantation labour rather than ancestral connection. While these articulations center the role of work in the production of plantation and post-plantation identifies, they simultaneously obscure the egregious exploitation of Indigenous Kānaka Maoli under the plantation regime and the broader settler-colonial order that endures in Hawai‘i as American-occupied territory (Day & Hogue 2019).
zh: 最后，种植园制度所催生的社会群体、集体身份与共同想象，也包含原住民性的表达和实践；它们在不同时空中被杂糅、争夺、重新主张，并变得异质。例如，在殖民时期的美国南部，19世纪初的反种植园起义与反叛，由黑人塞米诺尔人领导。这一人群形成于原住民社群与逃离奴役的非洲人之间的跨族裔联盟：原住民群体接纳了他们，双方联合起来，在第二次塞米诺尔战争（1835—1842）中，发动了美国历史上原住民与黑人协同程度最高的起义（Covington 2001；Hatch 2012；Porter 2013）。塞米诺尔身份与抗争通过跨族裔团结而在历史上涌现，同后种植园时代的夏威夷形成对照；后者的身份形成与扎根主张，呈现出复杂得多的局面。在那里，占主导地位的原住民性表达，来自东亚裔美国人，其祖先曾被输入甘蔗单一种植区劳动。他们形成了一种主要以种植园劳动、而非祖先联系为基础的归属理解。这些表达，将劳动在种植园及后种植园身份生产中的作用置于中心，却同时遮蔽了种植园制度对卡纳卡毛利原住民的极端剥削，以及在作为美国占领领土的夏威夷延续的、更广泛的定居殖民秩序（Day & Hogue 2019）。
body.review: 底本此处作post-plantation identifies，按上下文应为identities，英文保留原拼写。“美国占领领土”为作者在本段采用的分析表述。

en: Indigeneity is also and differently at play in South Africa, where plantation developments are reconfiguring understandings of and claims to nativity among San People, or Bushmen, and white South Africans, or Afrikaans. For example, the transformation of hoodia – a succulent plant traditionally used by Indigenous San as an appetite suppressant, energy enhancer, and breastfeeding aid – into a popular product of the global diet industry has been accompanied by processes of scientific research, patent ownership, contractual benefit-sharing mechanisms, and bioprospecting legislation that have created opportunities for San People to articulate their claims to ownership, intellectual property, and self-determination (Foster 2017). The case of rooibos, meanwhile, illustrates how the cultivation of a crop celebrated as ‘ecologically indigenous’ by people of ‘white’ African Indigeneity (in contrast to the ‘coloureds’) conjures new, plant-based expressions of belonging and exclusion (Ives 2017). Instead of grounding their sense of rootedness to place, rooibos cultivators find possibilities in and metonymic identification with rooibos – an indigenous plant – and with rooibos farming, thus articulating not only a claim to the past but also to the future, achieved through engagement in the lucrative rooibos industry.
zh: 原住民性也以另一种方式作用于南非：种植园开发正在重塑桑人——或称布须曼人——以及南非白人（Afrikaans）对本土性的理解与主张。例如，胡迪亚（hoodia）是一种多肉植物，桑人传统上将其用于抑制食欲、增强精力和辅助哺乳；如今，它转变为全球减肥产业的流行产品。这一转变伴随着科学研究、专利所有权、合同式利益分享机制和生物勘探立法等过程，为桑人表达对所有权、知识产权与自决的主张，创造了机会（Foster 2017）。与此同时，路易波士（rooibos）的例子揭示：自认具有“白人”非洲原住民性的人群——区别于“有色人”——栽培一种被赞为“生态本土物种”的作物，如何催生以植物为基础的新归属与排斥表达（Ives 2017）。路易波士种植者不是将扎根感奠基于地方，而是在路易波士这种本土植物及其种植业中寻找可能性，并与之形成转喻式的身份认同。由此，他们不仅提出对过去的主张，也通过参与利润丰厚的路易波士产业，实现对未来的主张。
body.review: Afrikaans通常是语言名称，底本在此用来称人群，英文照录；此处不据其写法把全部南非白人等同于单一族群。胡迪亚的传统用途是作者转述，非本译稿作出的药效认定。

en: At the same time, Indigenous emergences prompted by plantation proliferation are often diverse and conflicted (Roberts 2019). In Papua New Guinea, for instance, struggles over land, resources, and development are increasingly polarizing migrants and landowners, resulting in episodic tensions and violence across the palm oil sector (Koczberski & Curry 2004). Despite this, many customary landowners have been successful in maintaining an indigenous, though partly modified, system of land tenure that remains grounded in place-based social practices and values imbued with indigenous moralities (Curry & Koczberski 2009; Tammisto 2019). Land retains its traditional meaning as a source of history, identity, rootedness, and sacrality, but is now also understood and worked upon by Indigenous communities as resource and commodity (Tammisto 2024). As such, disagreements over the promise and perils of monocrop development are often disagreements over how to engage with, and benefit from, the plantation industry, while also preserving or establishing socially productive relations, both with other people, and with the land itself.
zh: 与此同时，种植园扩散所促成的原住民性涌现，往往多样而充满冲突（Roberts 2019）。例如，在巴布亚新几内亚，围绕土地、资源与发展的斗争，日益使移民与土地所有者分化，在棕榈油产业中造成间歇性的紧张和暴力（Koczberski & Curry 2004）。尽管如此，许多习惯法土地所有者，仍成功维持了一套虽部分改变、却属于原住民的土地权属制度。它依然扎根于植根地方的社会实践与价值，并浸润着原住民道德观（Curry & Koczberski 2009；Tammisto 2019）。土地保留了作为历史、身份、扎根感和神圣性来源的传统意义，但如今，原住民社群也将其理解为资源和商品，并据此经营（Tammisto 2024）。因此，围绕单一种植开发的希望与危险的分歧，往往涉及：如何参与种植园产业并从中获益，同时保留或建立具有社会生产力的关系——既与其他人，也与土地本身。

en: 4.4 Art and Aesthetics
zh: 4.4　艺术与美学

en: Our final foray into Plantationocenic emergence centres on art and aesthetics as political critique, creative resistance, social protest, and practice of repair, fashioned and transmitted by those subject to plantation regimes and their conjoined racial and ecological violence. In the realm of music, the connections between artistic expression and plantation histories are perhaps nowhere as palpable as in the blues, a genre that emerged in the post-emancipation, segregated American South, and that is rooted in the field hollers, work songs, and ballads composed and improvised by enslaved plantation workers (Bindas 1992). Blues songs took the form of rhythmic call-and-response chants and accompanied the harsh yet tedious monotony of plantation labour – and later, that of forced penal labour on Black prison farms. While blues songs were often encouraged by plantation owners for their positive effects on the stamina and productivity of the enslaved at work, their lyrics often contained concealed or cryptic critiques, condemnations, and even mockery of the plantation system and its White agents, in what might be described as a form of lyrical resistance. A central influence on African-American jazz and related musical currents, these songs represent one facet of the broader phenomenon that Clyde Woods (1998: 17) terms ‘blues epistemology’, or the Black revolutionary consciousness vested in the deconstruction of plantation relations.
zh: 我们对种植园世之涌现的最后一次探察，聚焦于作为政治批判、创造性抵抗、社会抗议及修复实践的艺术与美学。它们由承受种植园制度及其相互关联的种族和生态暴力的人们塑造、传递。在音乐领域，也许没有什么比布鲁斯更鲜明地体现了艺术表达与种植园历史之间的联系。布鲁斯诞生于奴隶解放后实行种族隔离的美国南部，根源在于被奴役的种植园工人创作和即兴演唱的田间呼号、劳动歌曲与叙事歌谣（Bindas 1992）。布鲁斯歌曲采用富有节奏的一呼一应形式，伴随着种植园劳动艰辛而乏味的单调节律；后来，也伴随着黑人监狱农场的强制刑罚劳动。种植园主常因布鲁斯有助于提高被奴役者劳动时的耐力和生产率而鼓励歌唱，但歌词中往往包含对种植园体系及其白人施行者隐蔽、隐晦的批评、谴责，甚至嘲弄，可说是一种歌词中的抵抗。这些歌曲深刻影响了非裔美国爵士乐及相关音乐潮流，也代表了一个更广泛现象的侧面：克莱德·伍兹（Clyde Woods 1998: 17）称其为“布鲁斯认识论”，即寄寓于对种植园关系进行解构之中的黑人革命意识。

en: Invocations of workers’ native lands, plants, and communities, as well as references to non-humans of the New World, were prevalent within plantation blues across the Black Atlantic, which often entailed a synthesis of African and European musical forms (Nunn 2016). In the early twentieth-century Mississippi Delta, for example, Black tenant farmers created a vast body of so-called ‘boll weevil songs’ that centred on a deadly pest that would eventually devastate the cotton industry. The lyrics of these songs conjured the boll weevil as a mobile, defiant, and resilient organism in constant search of a home, its invasive spread threatening the cotton sector at the same time as it mirrored the spirit of tenants whose frequent migrations were, not unlike those of the weevil, often driven by the pursuit of better opportunities (Giesen 2011). In this respect, boll weevil songs were as much about learning to live with cotton parasites as they were about Black tenants’ precarious positioning within cotton culture itself.
zh: 在黑色大西洋各地的种植园布鲁斯中，呼唤工人的原乡、植物与社群，以及提及新世界的非人存在，十分常见；这些音乐往往综合了非洲与欧洲的音乐形式（Nunn 2016）。例如，在20世纪初的密西西比三角洲，黑人佃农创作了大量所谓“棉铃象甲之歌”，围绕一种最终将摧毁棉花产业的致命害虫展开。歌词将棉铃象甲塑造成一种不断寻找家园、流动不居、桀骜而坚韧的生物；它的入侵性扩散威胁着棉花产业，同时也映照出佃农的精神：佃农频繁迁移，与象甲相似，也往往是为了追求更好的机会（Giesen 2011）。从这个意义上说，棉铃象甲之歌既关乎学会与棉花寄生生物共处，也关乎黑人佃农在棉花文化本身之中的不稳定处境。

en: A different multispecies edge to plantation-inspired, emergent musical forms manifests in the ‘Black Pacific’ (Webb-Gannon & Webb 2018; Webb & Webb-Gannon 2020). While Melanesians have long sought to distance themselves from the ‘natural’ world due to colonial constructs that instrumentalized their Blackness to relegate them to a putative primitiveness, many lyrics from the region celebrate the more-than-human realm alternately as an Edenic, tropical paradise, as God’s gift to Melanesians and to the world, or as a source of wealth and identity plundered through extractive capitalism and colonialism.
zh: 在“黑色太平洋”，受种植园启发而涌现的音乐形式，展现了另一种多物种面向（Webb-Gannon & Webb 2018；Webb & Webb-Gannon 2020）。殖民观念曾利用美拉尼西亚人的黑肤色，把他们贬入一种被假定的原始状态，因此，他们长期试图与“自然”世界保持距离。然而，该地区许多歌词，却以不同方式礼赞超越人类的领域：或把它视为伊甸园般的热带乐土，或视为上帝赠予美拉尼西亚人与世界的礼物，或视为遭攫取性资本主义与殖民主义掠夺的财富和身份来源。

en: A powerful example of music as multispecies protest in the Black Pacific is the tradition of mourning songs practiced by Indigenous West Papuans on the oil palm frontier (Chao 2023b). Performed by men, women, and children near monocrops, roads, and razed forests, mourning songs, which began to spread following the arrival of palm, condemn and grieve the indiscriminate killing of native organisms due to monocrop developments while celebrating their meaningful pasts, histories, and kinships with local clans. Much like pidginized blues songs once acted as a veiled medium to communicate secret messages among the enslaved, so too Papuans describe multispecies mourning songs as a form of creative resistance and collective defiance – one that pushes against the disenchantment of plantation modernity through an insistence on storying and singing the lifeways and deathways of more-than-human beings subject to plantations’ ecocidal effects.
zh: 在黑色太平洋，音乐作为多物种抗议的一个有力例证，是西巴布亚原住民在油棕边疆实践的哀歌传统（Chao 2023b）。这些哀歌随着油棕到来而开始传播，由男人、女人与儿童在单一种植区、道路及夷平的森林附近演唱。它们谴责并哀悼单一种植开发对本土生物不加区分的杀戮，同时颂扬这些生物富有意义的往昔、历史，以及同当地氏族的亲属关系。正如使用皮钦语的布鲁斯歌曲，曾作为被奴役者之间传递秘密信息的隐蔽媒介，巴布亚人也将多物种哀歌视为创造性抵抗与集体抗争：它坚持讲述和歌唱那些承受种植园生态灭绝效应的超越人类存在的生与死，以此反抗种植园现代性的祛魅。

en: Alongside music, the reconceptualization of human subjecthood through the animacy of non-human forces runs through literary works focused upon or inspired by plantation lifeworlds and afterlives. In the United States, this is visible in the vast body of poems, novels, and memoirs produced by African-American descendants of enslaved plantation workers across the twentieth century and beyond. As expressions of the ‘Black radical imagination’ (Kelley 2002), these oeuvres collectively constitute what Christina Sharpe (2016) calls ‘wake work’, or counter-hegemonic sites of Black artistic production, resistance, consciousness, and possibility that address the ‘monstrous intimacies’ of slavery and their repetition in the form of post-slavery Black subjectivity (see also Sharpe 2010).
zh: 除了音乐，通过非人力量的活性重新理解人类主体地位，也是聚焦种植园生活世界及其后续存续、或从中得到启发的文学作品的一条贯穿线索。在美国，从20世纪延续至今，由被奴役种植园工人的非裔美国后代创作的大量诗歌、小说和回忆录，体现了这一点。作为“黑人激进想象”的表达（Kelley 2002），这些作品共同构成了克里斯蒂娜·夏普（Christina Sharpe 2016）所谓的“守醒工作”（wake work）：黑人艺术生产、抵抗、意识与可能性的反霸权场域，直面奴隶制的“怪诞亲密关系”，及其在奴隶制之后的黑人主体性中的重复（另见Sharpe 2010）。
body.review: wake work暂译“守醒工作”；wake兼有守灵、清醒与船只尾流等意涵，不能仅理解为一般的纪念活动。

en: Paul Laurence Dunbar’s plantation poems and W. E. B. Du Bois’s

offer powerful examples of how Black intellectuals have reimagined the plantation landscape as animate matter, capable of storing memory, articulating pain, and enabling defiance (McInnis 2016; Child 2019). In Du Bois’s novel, the ‘black soil’ of former plantation landscapes becomes a fecund ground for radical freedom and independence, its capacity to anchor collective autonomy inseparable from the recognition of Black landownership. Darkness, likewise, operates as a more-than-human force within the work, as exemplified by the strange music that rises from murky swamps and Black bodies. Resignified as a quality rather than a deficiency, darkness in the novel further acquires tactical value in enabling black invisibility during mob attacks, exemplifying a repurposing of racial hypervisibility into a resource of protection. In both respects, soil and darkness are positioned as active collaborators in Black life-making, charged with generative and resistant potential. Dunbar’s poetry, meanwhile, turns to haunted landscapes in which trees and soils register the afterlives of plantation violence. One example is ‘The Haunted Oak’ (1903), which stages a dialogue with a lynching tree whose bark absorbs the agony of a murdered black man and whose testimony survives where human voices are forcefully muted. The tree’s spectral utterances collapse distinctions between subject and object and human and vegetal, indicting regimes of ownership that once fused White control of over bodies, labour, and land. The non-human emerges as both archive and witness, bearing the imprint of racial violence. Foregrounding soil, darkness, and trees as co-actors, Du Bois and Dunbar’s works refuse to confine plantations to a histories of subjugation. Instead, these works recast plantations and their ecological and material residues as sites of agropolitical possibility in the making of a Black subjecthood that is grounded in the embrace of cross-species entanglements and the recognition of the political vitality of the non-human.
zh: 保罗·劳伦斯·邓巴的种植园诗歌，以及W. E. B. 杜波依斯的《银羊毛的追寻》（The Quest of the Silver Fleece），有力地说明了黑人知识分子如何将种植园景观重新想象为有生命的物质，能够储存记忆、表达痛苦，并使抗争成为可能（McInnis 2016；Child 2019）。在杜波依斯的小说中，昔日种植园景观的“黑土”，成为激进自由与独立的肥沃土壤；它支撑集体自治的能力，与承认黑人土地所有权密不可分。黑暗也作为一种超越人类的力量作用于作品之中：从幽暗沼泽与黑人身体升起的奇异音乐，便是例证。小说把黑暗重新赋义为一种特质，而非一种缺陷；它还获得了战术价值，使黑人在暴徒袭击时能够隐身，将因种族而过度显眼的处境转化为保护资源。在这两个方面，土壤与黑暗都成为黑人营造生活的积极合作者，蕴含生成与抵抗的潜能。邓巴的诗歌则转向幽灵萦绕的景观，其中，树木与土壤记录着种植园暴力的后续存续。一个例子是《闹鬼的橡树》（The Haunted Oak，1903）：诗中与一棵曾用于私刑的树展开对话，树皮吸收了一名被杀黑人的痛苦；在人声被强制压制之处，树的证词仍然留存。树的幽灵般话语，消解了主体与客体、人类与植物的区分，控诉曾将白人对身体、劳动与土地的控制融为一体的所有权制度。非人同时成为档案与见证，承载着种族暴力的印记。杜波依斯与邓巴将土壤、黑暗和树木置为共同的行动者，拒绝把种植园仅仅局限于征服史。相反，他们把种植园及其生态和物质残留，重新塑造为具有农业政治可能性的场所，参与建构一种黑人主体地位：其基础是拥抱跨物种纠缠，并承认非人的政治活力。
body.review: 本段底本有control of over、a histories等语法问题，英文照录，中文按上下文译出。作品中文题名为本稿工作译名。

en: Non-human actors and forces figure in plantation-inspired literary works produced across many other world geographies beyond the Black Atlantic, where monocrops have also radically reshaped multispecies pasts, presents, and futures. In the Latin American context, for instance, Argentinian author Samanta Schweblin’s award-winning novel
(2017, originally published in 2014 in Spanish as

) deploys magical realism and ecohorror to story the toxic contamination of water bodies from chemical pesticides used in soy plantations and its subsequent connections with birth defects, neurological imbalances, and fertility problems, in a haunting tale of anthropogenic monstrosity replete with deformed beings, poisoned animals, dystopic futures, and collapsing ecologies (Sarkar 2023). Fijian authors Totaram Sanadhya’s ‘The Story of the Haunted Line’ (1922) and Subramani’s ‘The Fantasy Eaters’ (1988) lean into sugarcane plantations in the gothic mode, bringing to life the slow violence of food insecurity caused by monocrop developments, the threats of mosquito-borne diseases, the exhaustion of human and environmental fertility, the disciplining of life into cheap energy, the multispecies labour regimes of the monocrop, and the ghostly social, economic, and environmental legacies of plantation lifeworlds (Vandertop 2020). Indian author and film-maker Satyajit Ray, meanwhile, delves into the haunting horrors of colonial plantations in his short story ‘Indigo’ (1968), which blurs the line between the real and supernatural through the recounting of a young Indian man who is possessed by the spirit and body of a nineteenth-century English plantation owner and tax lord while overnighting in an abandoned bungalow in the indigo-producing Bengalese district of Birbhum. In Amitav Ghosh’s

(2021), the parable offers a powerful stylistic form for uncovering historical continuities and connections between climate change and the decimation of indigenous forests and populations to establish nutmeg plantations for the European market in the Dutch-occupied Banda Islands. Both colonial violence and contemporary planetary crises, Ghosh demonstrates, remain rooted in an imperial mindset wherein the Earth exists solely as a resource for profit, and its exploitation continues to contribute to environmental degradation and social inequality.
zh: 在黑色大西洋之外的许多地区，单一种植同样剧烈重塑了多物种的过去、现在与未来；那些受种植园启发的文学作品，也呈现非人行动者与力量。例如，在拉丁美洲，阿根廷作家萨曼塔·施韦布林的获奖小说《发热之梦》（Fever Dream，2017；2014年以西班牙语题名Distancia de rescate初版），以魔幻现实主义和生态恐怖，讲述大豆种植园使用的化学农药对水体造成的有毒污染，以及它随后同出生缺陷、神经失衡和生育问题的联系。这是一个由人类造成的怪物性不断萦绕的故事，充斥畸形存在、中毒动物、反乌托邦未来，以及崩溃的生态（Sarkar 2023）。斐济作家托塔拉姆·萨纳迪亚的《闹鬼工棚的故事》（The Story of the Haunted Line，1922），以及苏布拉马尼的《吞食幻想者》（The Fantasy Eaters，1988），以哥特式手法进入甘蔗种植园，将下列现象活现于纸上：单一种植开发造成的食物不安全所带来的缓慢暴力、蚊媒疾病的威胁、人类生育能力与环境肥力的耗竭、生命被规训为廉价能源、单一种植的多物种劳动制度，以及种植园生活世界如幽灵般延续的社会、经济与环境遗产（Vandertop 2020）。印度作家、电影人萨蒂亚吉特·雷伊，则在短篇小说《靛蓝》（Indigo，1968）中探究殖民种植园挥之不去的恐怖：一名年轻印度男子，在产靛蓝的孟加拉比尔布姆地区一座废弃平房中过夜，被一位19世纪英国种植园主兼征税领主的灵与身体附占；故事模糊了现实与超自然的界线。在阿米塔夫·高希的《肉豆蔻的诅咒》（The Nutmeg Curse，2021）中，寓言成为有力的文体形式，揭示气候变化与如下历史之间的连续性及联系：荷兰占领的班达群岛，为给欧洲市场建立肉豆蔻种植园，本土森林与人口遭到毁灭性摧残。高希表明，殖民暴力与当代行星危机，都仍植根于帝国心态：大地只作为获利资源而存在，对它的剥削持续促成环境恶化与社会不平等。
body.review: 本段文学作品的中文题名用于对照阅读，均附底本英文题名，不据此声称沿用正式中译本书名。

en: Beyond the realm of literature, creative modes of storying plantations are now also seeping into the realm of scholarly writing, as exemplified by anthropologist Michael Taussig’s
(2018), which speaks to the ravaging impacts of monocrop oil palm plantations in Colombia (Chao 2019). Described by Taussig as ‘animistic writing’ or ‘ethnographic (sur)realism’,

is populated by a panoply of human and non-human actors: from paramilitaries, peasants, and activists to cows, cocaine, and cash crops that entangle with swamps, migrant camps, polluted rivers, braying donkeys, and ancient Indian fields. ‘Thought-images’ in the form of introspective musings, hand-drawn pictures, and uncaptioned photographs, delve into the sounds and atmospheres of industrial monocrops, desolate oil palm towns, and dying forests. The amorphous narrative of the text jolts the reader from the empirical to the reflexive, the violent to the mundane, and the human to the other-than-human. In embracing the magic and madness of plantation violence,

counters what Taussig (2015) terms ‘agribusiness writing’, or a form of writing that, like the plantation system itself, is stripped of its capacity to provoke surprise and wonder and thus entrenches the dangerous fiction of human mastery over multispecies realities.
zh: 在文学之外，创造性讲述种植园的方式，如今也渗入学术写作。人类学家迈克尔·陶西格的《非洲棕榈》（Palma Africana，2018）便是例子，它讲述哥伦比亚单一油棕种植园的破坏性影响（Chao 2019）。陶西格将其称为“泛灵论写作”或“民族志的（超）现实主义”。书中充满各种人类与非人行动者：从准军事人员、农民和活动人士，到牛、可卡因与经济作物；它们同沼泽、移民营地、受污染的河流、嘶鸣的驴，以及古老的印第安农田纠缠在一起。以自省思绪、手绘图画和无图注照片为形式的“思想—图像”，深入探察工业单一种植区、荒凉油棕城镇和垂死森林的声音与氛围。文本不定形的叙述，让读者在经验与反思、暴力与日常、人类与非人之间骤然转换。《非洲棕榈》拥抱种植园暴力中的魔法与疯狂，以此反击陶西格（2015）所谓的“农业企业式写作”：那种写作，与种植园体系本身一样，被剥去了激起意外与惊奇的能力，因而巩固了人类能够主宰多物种现实这一危险虚构。

en: Finally, numerous examples of plantation and counter-plantation imaginaries can be found in the realm of the visual and performative arts. In the American context, one might think of Brooklyn-based Jamaican photographer Radcliffe Roye’s award-winning 2016 photograph, ‘Don’t Shoot!’, which portrays a young man of colour holding his hands up in a field of white cotton, and which was taken near Clarksdale, Mississippi, soon after the police killings of African-American teenagers Michael Brown and Eric Garner. The image is one of 4,000 photos linking the enduring social legacies of plantations in the American South, including ongoing Black American experiences of racial terror, segregation, surveillance, and policing (Aikens et al. 2019). Or, one might envision African-American painter Kara Walker’s Brooklyn 2014 installation, ‘A Subtlety: or the Marvelous Sugar Baby’, which features a colossal nude sphinx sculpted from foam and coated with refined sugar, surrounded by smaller figures of children cast in brown sugar and molasses who appear to melt into the floor of the former sugar refinery where the installation is located. The work evokes the intertwined histories of sugar plantations, capitalism, enslavement, labour, violence, racism, and desire, exposing how White consumption depended on plantation commodities and Black suffering.
zh: 最后，在视觉和表演艺术领域，也有许多种植园与反种植园想象的例子。在美国，人们可能想到定居布鲁克林的牙买加摄影师拉德克利夫·罗伊的获奖摄影作品《别开枪！》（Don’t Shoot!，2016）：画面中，一名有色人种青年在洁白的棉田里举起双手。照片拍摄于密西西比州克拉克斯代尔附近，时间是在非裔美国青少年迈克尔·布朗和埃里克·加纳遭警察杀害之后不久。这张照片属于一个四千张照片的系列，关联着美国南部种植园延续至今的社会遗产，包括美国黑人持续经历的种族恐怖、隔离、监视与警务控制（Aikens et al. 2019）。人们也可能想到非裔美国画家卡拉·沃克2014年在布鲁克林的装置作品《精巧之物：或奇妙的糖宝贝》（A Subtlety: or the Marvelous Sugar Baby）。它呈现一尊以泡沫塑形、表面覆着精制白糖的巨大裸体斯芬克斯，周围环绕着以红糖和糖蜜铸成的小型儿童像；这些儿童仿佛正融化进装置所在的昔日炼糖厂地板。作品唤起糖业种植园、资本主义、奴役、劳动、暴力、种族主义和欲望相互纠缠的历史，揭露白人消费如何依赖种植园商品与黑人的苦难。
body.review: 底本将布朗与加纳并称青少年有误：加纳2014年去世时43岁，布朗18岁，可与美国国会H.Res.589提出文本所列年龄核对。底本照片年份2016保留，未将刊载／获奖年份与实际拍摄年份混为已核实事实。

en: Further south in Latin America, contemporary Cuban artists have harnessed the conceptual, political, and aesthetic power of intermediality, or the use of multi-layered mediums and techniques, to represent the symbolic and social afterlives of sugar plantations (Sklodowska 2022). For instance, Tania Bruguera’s performance,

), in which she ate soil mixed with salt water for forty-five minutes, evokes Indigenous Taíno resistance under Spanish colonization, which often involved the symbolic ingestion of soil, while also conjuring the horrific bodily punishment and iron-mask muzzling of enslaved plantation workers who sought to suicide by consuming dirt. The dehumanization of Black people turned instruments of colonial capitalism, meanwhile, is vividly captured in the photography of Reinaldo Echemendía Cid, and particularly in

). In this striking image, a stretched out, naked, muscular Afro-Cuban man acts as a coupling rod holding together the wheels of an antique train, his power and labour standing in for the locomotive’s engines and his energy metabolized to accelerate production. The photograph speaks both to the herculean strength of the enslaved and to their reduction to expendable and interchangeable cogs, instruments, and automatons within the profit-making plantation machine.
zh: 再往南到拉丁美洲，古巴当代艺术家借助跨媒介性——即使用多层媒介与技法——的概念、政治和美学力量，表现糖业种植园在象征与社会层面的后续存续（Sklodowska 2022）。例如，塔尼娅·布鲁格拉的行为作品《负罪之重》（El Peso de la Culpa，1997—1999），让她在四十五分钟里吞食混有盐水的泥土。它唤起西班牙殖民统治下泰诺原住民的抵抗，其中常包括象征性地吞食泥土；它也唤起对那些试图通过食土自杀的被奴役种植园工人施行的可怖肉体惩罚，以及用铁面具封嘴的做法。与此同时，黑人被变成殖民资本主义工具的非人化过程，鲜明地呈现在雷纳尔多·埃切门迪亚·西德的摄影中，尤其是《联—牵引》（Con-tracción，2015）。在这张震撼的照片里，一名肌肉健壮、赤身伸展的非裔古巴男子，充当连接古老火车车轮的连杆；他的力量与劳动替代了机车引擎，他的能量经由代谢，用来加速生产。这张照片既表达了被奴役者如大力神般的力量，也表达了他们在获利的种植园机器中，被降格为可耗用、可替换的齿轮、工具和自动机的处境。

en: Another lens into plantation lifeworlds is offered by those visual artworks and performances that centre the multispecies intimacies, memories, and connections that were borne of, or that survived despite, the rise and wake of monoculture landscapes. Exemplifying this is Cuban artist Carlos Martiel’s performance,
), that invokes and celebrates African-descendant spirituality through bodily mediated and empowering ties with the earth. Performed at Cuba’s Academia de Artes Plásticas San Alejandro,

features Martiel, dressed in white, kneeling on the lawn and engraving the Nyansapo symbol of West African wisdom into the grass using his tongue. The work reframes the earth as a medium of healing and ancestral communion, at the same time as it honours the resilience of enslaved peoples who trans-formed materials such as mud, clay, plants, bones, and ash into artistic and spiritual creativity and connection. In a similar vein, Malaysian artist Shooshie Sulaiman’s
) and

), displayed at the Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art in Nusantara in Jakarta, draw on her cherished memories of growing up on a rubber plantation to challenge representations of the Malaysian rubber landscape solely as a colonial and capitalist space (Aroisoaie 2025). Instead, Sulaiman’s art installations reclaim rubber as tradition, home, playground, kin, and education, creatively teasing out the ambivalent legacy of rubber in Malaysia as simultaneously charged with painful tensions and productive possibilities. Both pieces gesture towards the process of becoming-with rubber through an aesthetics of immersion that opens creative pathways for decolonial ways of living in and with plantations as sites of unexpected multispecies relatedness. The theme of plantationocenic immersion explored in Sulaiman’s art finds resonance in Singapore-born artist Simryn Gill’s photograph series,

(1999), in which Gill masks and disguises herself as a range of plants to naturalize human figures into the landscape. Shots of Gill in a monocrop oil palm plantation, holding a huge oil palm fruit bunch, her head composed of blurry oil palm fronds, conjure the vengeful alien plants of Cold War sci-fi imaginaries. At the same time, they symbolize an epoch wherein palm oil’s ubiquity in foods and commodities worldwide is effectively bringing all of us together in a global process of ‘becoming palm’ (Gill & Taussig 2017).
zh: 还有一些视觉艺术作品与行为表演，将多物种的亲密、记忆与联系置于中心，为理解种植园生活世界提供了另一种视角。这些关系，或诞生于单一种植景观的兴起及其余波之中，或尽管遭遇这种兴起与余波，仍然存续。古巴艺术家卡洛斯·马蒂埃尔的行为作品《智慧》（Sabiduría，1989）便是例证：它通过身体媒介促成的、赋予力量的与大地的纽带，唤起并礼赞非洲裔的精神世界。作品在古巴圣亚历杭德罗美术学院表演，马蒂埃尔身穿白衣，跪在草地上，用舌头在草地刻出象征西非智慧的Nyansapo符号。作品把大地重新理解为疗愈与祖先交流的媒介，同时致敬被奴役者的韧性：他们将泥土、黏土、植物、骨头与灰烬等材料，转化为艺术和精神上的创造与联系。与此相近，马来西亚艺术家舒希·苏莱曼的《橡胶幼儿园》（Tadika Getah，2019）和《橡胶景观》（Main Getah／Rubberscape，2019），在雅加达努山塔拉现当代艺术博物馆展出，取材于她珍爱的橡胶种植园成长记忆，挑战把马来西亚橡胶景观仅仅表现为殖民和资本主义空间的做法（Aroisoaie 2025）。相反，苏莱曼的艺术装置，把橡胶重新认作传统、家园、游乐场、亲属与教育，创造性地梳理马来西亚橡胶遗产的矛盾性：它既充满痛苦张力，也富于生成的可能。两件作品都通过沉浸美学，指向与橡胶共同生成的过程，为去殖民的生活方式开辟创造性路径：生活于种植园之中，并与之共同生活，将其视为出人意料的多物种亲缘关系的场所。苏莱曼艺术中探究的种植园世沉浸主题，与出生于新加坡的艺术家西姆琳·吉尔的摄影系列《植被》（Vegetation，1999）形成共鸣。在这个系列中，吉尔将自己遮蔽、伪装成多种植物，让人形融入自然景观。在单一油棕种植园中，她抱着巨大的油棕果串，头部由模糊的油棕叶构成；这些照片，唤起冷战科幻想象中复仇的异星植物。同时，它们也象征了一个时代：棕榈油在全世界食物与商品中的无所不在，正切实地把我们所有人联结起来，纳入一个全球性的“成为棕榈”过程（Gill & Taussig 2017）。
body.review: 底本《智慧》年份作1989；古根海姆博物馆的作品介绍记为2007，且描述用牙齿拔草，而底本作舌头刻画，此处照录并注明差异。本段Aroisoaie在作者本人及论文署名中为Arosoaie。作品中文名均为工作译名。

en: 4.5 Conclusions
zh: 4.5　结论

en: The plantation-spurred material transformations, socio-ecological relations, and epistemic cross-pollinations examined in this section offer valuable empirical and conceptual insights into the contexts and contours of emergence as ‘the appearance of unprecedented relational properties, which are not reducible to any of the more basic component parts that give rise to them’ (Kohn 2015: 166). Across the realms of illness and healing, vegetal ontologies, identities and imaginaries, and art and aesthetics, new lifeworlds have emerged at the sites where former ones have been displaced or disfigured, engendering new modes of communing with matter, species, and ecosystems, as well as new ways of sustaining life in the long shadow of plantation regimes. At the same time, it is important to remind ourselves that emergence has not always nor necessarily been emancipatory and anti-speciesist in its thrust and pull. Just as plantations have given rise to counter-hegemonic understandings and practices of more-than-human future-building, so too have they been the font of anthropocentric, racializing, and instrumentalizing processes anchored in the exploitation of bodies and beings in the name of science, medicine, and progress.
zh: 本部分考察的、由种植园推动的物质转化、社会—生态关系与认识论的相互交融，为理解涌现的情境与轮廓，提供了有价值的经验和概念洞见。涌现是“前所未有的关系属性的出现，而这些属性不能还原为任何使其产生的更基本构成部分”（Kohn 2015: 166）。在疾病与疗愈、植物本体论、身份与想象，以及艺术与美学等领域，新的生活世界，在旧世界被驱离或毁损之处涌现，产生了与物质、物种和生态系统交流的新方式，也产生了在种植园制度漫长阴影下维系生命的新方式。与此同时，我们也必须提醒自己：涌现的推动方向，并非总是、也不必然是解放性的和反物种主义的。正如种植园催生了建构超越人类未来的反霸权理解与实践，它也孕育了以人类为中心、施行种族化与工具化的过程；这些过程，以科学、医学和进步之名，扎根于对身体与生命存在的剥削。

en: To think with emergences across historical, cultural, and epistemic contexts helps draw attention to the different ethico-moral valences and eco-social consequences of knowledge production across the uneven power fields within which it takes place, takes hold, and meets resistance. It points to the continuously shifting ontological and representational grounds of plantations as multispecies contact zones where the emergence of new political and cultural figurations is tethered to the fates and futures, real and speculative, of both human and non-human actors. It also uncovers in agro-industrial landscapes unexpected possibilities for acts of collective and creative defiance that range from sweeping social movements to everyday acts of little justice. Taken together, these forms of defiance offer vital avenues for reckoning with the uneven conditions of more-than-human liveability that shape plantation lifeworlds and afterlives.
zh: 借助不同历史、文化与认识论语境中的涌现来思考，有助于关注知识生产的不同伦理—道德意义，以及生态—社会后果；知识生产正是在不平等的权力场域中发生、扎根并遭遇抵抗。它指出，作为多物种接触地带，种植园的本体论与再现基础不断变化；在那里，新的政治与文化构成的涌现，同人类及非人行动者真实或推想的命运与未来相连。它也在农工业景观中，揭示了集体而富于创造性的抗争行动的意外可能：从席卷广泛的社会运动，到日常践行微小正义的行动。合在一起，这些抗争形式提供了关键途径，让我们直面塑造种植园生活世界及其后续存续的、超越人类生命得以存续的不平等条件。
